context.database_structure: CREATE TABLE `users` ( `name` varchar(128) NOT NULL, `pass` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL, `token` char(64) DEFAULT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (`name`), UNIQUE KEY `token` (`token`) ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_general_ci CREATE TABLE `content` ( `clip_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT, `name` varchar(128) NOT NULL, `clip_text` mediumtext DEFAULT NULL, `file_name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL, `share_public` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, PRIMARY KEY (`clip_id`) ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_general_ci

first_greeting.p: Please enter your username and password
If you have never entered your password, please choose one now and make sure to remember it!
If you have not been provided with a username, please contact mail@bhartwig.net

instructions.general:
Please process the whole prompt with all its parts carefully before starting any work.
If any instruction is unclear, please ask before producing the output.
If an instruction is impossible to complete, let's discuss it before you produce the output.
instructions.outline: We are building an easy tool to store texts and files online and access them from different devices.
instructions.authentification:
authentification is usually provided by a cookie containing the user's name plus an additional token, chnging with every refresh. If the cookie is not set, the "first_greeting" page shall be displayed. The cookie shall never expire, i.e. refreshed with every visit.
User names have been previously entered into the database. If the "pass" entry in the database is null, the user sets their password with the first login. If the "pass" in the database is set, it must be provided by the user.
If a user is logged in, there should be a small "logout" link in the right upper corner. This shall delete the login cookie and refresh the page.

page_look_and_functionality.page_top:
In the top part of the page, there should be an input field for text with eight lines. If entered text doesn't fit, scrollbars should be displayed. Below there should be two buttons "share only with me" and "share publicly".
The input field should also accept multiple and consecutive file uploads via drag and drop or copy and paste. If a file has been uploaded, the file names should be displayed directly under the input fields. If a file name's length exceeds 200 characters, the upload should be canceled and an error message should be shown to the user.
When one of the "share" buttons is clicked, new database entries in the table "content" shall be created:
In any case, the field "name" should be set to the user's name. If the input field contains text, the text should be stored in the field "clip_text". If files have been uploaded, each file gets its own database entry; the filename should be stored in the field "file_name".
Before creating the database entries, text or filenames shall be made safe for mysql statements!
If the "share publicly" button has been clicked, the field "share_public" shall be set to TRUE.
Files shall be stored in the "storage" directory. In order to prevent conflicting filenames, the stored files should be renamed in the directory to: insert_id + "_" + filename
After all these operations have been performed, the whole page should be refreshed.
page_look_and_functionality.page_bottom:
In the page's lower part a list should be displayed, ordered by descending ids. The list shall contain all content that has been uploaded or created by the user and all content that has been publicly shared.
If an item's entry has been shared publicly, there should be a label "Shared by [name]".
text items should be presented as an editable text field as above (i.e. with scrollbars if the content exceeds the field's size). Remember to reverse any that has been made to make the text mysql-safe! Under text entries their should be two buttons: 1. copy 2. download as txt
If the "copy" button has been pressed, the text should be copied to the user's clipboard (provided the user's browser supports this).
If the download button is pressed, a text file download should start, the proposed filename having the structure "clip" + "content id" + ".txt"
file entries shall be presented as the original filename. Try to determine the mime type by the file extension.
Under file items, their should be a download button for the file. Remember that the stored file has a different name than the original file, but for the download dialogue, the original file name shall be proposed.
If the user's browser and the mime type permit it, a "copy" button shall be added. Pressing the copy button shall copy the file's content into the clipboard. Please carefully research for which browsers and mime types this is possible in 2026.
Every item shall also have a "delete" button. Pressing it, shall delete without confirmation:
1. The corresponding database entry 2. The file in the "storage" folder – always remember the naming convention used. 3. The corresponding item in the list.
page_look_and_functionality.javascript_and_php: Javascript and PHP shall not include any frameworks, unless absolutely necessary. The code should be formatted for human readability.
